partners.mechanism_chain: NHS (HGNC:7820) —DISRUPTS→ lens fiber cell differentiation and maintenance (GO:0001849); NHS (HGNC:7820) —LEADS_TO→ Nance-Horan syndrome (MONDO:0010545); crystallin alpha B (HGNC:2592) —BINDS→ lens fiber cell differentiation and maintenance (GO:0001849); lens fiber cell differentiation and maintenance (GO:0001849) —LEADS_TO→ cataract 40 (MONDO:0010544). Mutations in the NHS gene lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting lens fiber cell differentiation and maintenance, ultimately causing Nance-Horan syndrome. Crystallin alpha B, a critical protein for lens clarity, is involved in these same cellular processes. Disruption of NHS function affects the cellular environment, impacting the stability and function of crystallin alpha B, leading to cataract 40.

Mutations in the NHS gene lead to haploinsufficiency, disrupting lens fiber cell differentiation and maintenance, ultimately causing Nance-Horan syndrome. Crystallin alpha B, a critical protein for lens clarity, is involved in these same cellular processes. Disruption of NHS function affects the cellular environment, impacting the stability and function of crystallin alpha B, leading to cataract 40.

**How to falsify it:** The absence of mutations in the NHS gene in patients with cataract 40, or identification of a distinct causal gene for cataract 40 with no functional overlap with NHS, would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, if NHS mutations in patients with cataract 40 consistently show a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect, it would contradict the proposed haploinsufficiency mechanism. _(variant: Common variants (AF > 0.01) in the NHS gene associated with cataract 40 would suggest a non-causal role or incomplete penetrance.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of NHS in both Nance-Horan syndrome and cataract 40 could lead to the development of targeted therapies for lens opacities, potentially benefiting patients with either condition. Investigating the interaction between NHS and crystallin alpha B may reveal new therapeutic targets for preventing or treating cataracts.
